title: Hp500Comparison
description: Catalog row hp500-comparison 1.0.1: the paired comparison of the held-out forecasting methods on the ten HP500 surveys, written by data-pipeline/pipeline/hp500/comparison.py to data/derived/hp500/comparison.json from hp500-loo and, when present, hp500-crusherbayes (read only). Per measured target (throughput tph [t/h], power kW [kW]): the measured values, every method with its document MAPE and its ten held-out absolute percent errors, the recommended method (the lowest document MAPE among the methods that are not controls) and the runner-up (the next lowest), and for every method with predictions its paired difference against the recommended one: d_i = APE_i(method) - APE_i(recommended) in percentage points (positive: the method is worse), the mean of d, its 95 percent percentile bootstrap interval over the surveys (numpy.random.default_rng(seed).integers(0, n, size=(resamples, n)), the mean of d over each resample, the 2.5 and 97.5 percent quantiles: the resampling of the CrusherBayes manuscript), wins (the surveys where the recommended method has the strictly lower APE) and p_better (the share of resamples whose mean is above 0). The label-shuffle control has no per-survey predictions and carries no paired row. With hp500-crusherbayes absent, crusherbayes.included is false, its note says so and no CrusherBayes row appears. Rules the schema cannot state, checked by the producer test: n equals the length of every per-survey list; recommended and runner_up name methods that are not controls, recommended has the lowest mape_pct and runner_up the next; every paired row's against is the recommended method; ci95 low is at most mean_diff_pts and high at least it; the document is byte-identical for the same inputs. Derived from data licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://doi.org/10.3390/min14090919).

source.description: The source publication of the surveys (Rocha, Campos, Silva and Tavares 2024), as the survey reader states it.

engine_version.description: The product version that wrote the document (format X.XX.XXX); a version other than VERSION makes the row stale.

n.description: The number of surveys paired (ten in the committed build); every per-survey list has this length.

method.description: The resampling in words: a percentile bootstrap over the surveys of the mean paired difference.

resamples.description: The number B of bootstrap resamples of the survey indices (20,000 in the committed build).

seed.description: The seed of numpy.random.default_rng that draws the resampled survey indices (42).

quantiles.description: The lower and upper percentiles of the 95 percent interval, 2.5 and 97.5 [%].

bootstrap.description: How the paired intervals are resampled: the resampling of the CrusherBayes manuscript.

loo.description: The CrusherCal held-out document (hp500-loo) the predictions are read from.

crusherbayes.description: The CrusherBayes document (hp500-crusherbayes) when it is in the build; null when it is absent.

inputs.description: The two documents the comparison is computed from, with their schema and product version.

included.description: True when the CrusherBayes document is present and sampled on the same surveys, so its rows are paired.

note.description: Why CrusherBayes is not compared (its document is absent or was sampled on other surveys); null when it is included.

crusherbayes.description: Whether CrusherBayes takes part in the comparison.

tph.description: The comparison on the measured throughput, errors in percent of the measured t/h.

kW.description: The comparison on the measured power, errors in percent of the measured kW.

targets.description: The comparison per measured target: throughput (tph) and power (kW).

text.description: A reader-facing string in English and Spanish.

path.description: The input's path relative to data/derived.

schema.description: The schema identifier the input document declares.

engine_version.description: The product version that wrote the input document.

input.description: One input document: where it is, its schema and the product version that wrote it.

series.description: One value per survey, in survey order.

id.description: The method's key as its source document stores it: a key of the strict block of hp500-loo, or crusherbayes.

control.description: True for a control (the constant mean and the label shuffle), which is never recommended.

mape_pct.description: The method's held-out MAPE as its source document states it [%].

ape_pct.description: The held-out absolute percentage error at each survey, in survey order; null for the label shuffle, whose per-survey predictions no document stores [%].

method.description: One method compared on the target: its identifier, whether it is a control, its MAPE and its per-survey errors.

against.description: The method it is compared against: always the recommended method of the target.

mean_diff_pts.description: The mean over the surveys of d_i = APE_i(method) - APE_i(recommended); positive when the method is worse [points].

ci95.description: The 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of the mean of d over the bootstrap resamples: the 95 percent interval [points].

wins.description: The number of surveys on which the recommended method has the strictly lower absolute percentage error.

p_better.description: The share of resamples whose mean of d is above zero: how often the recommended method is better on average [fraction].

paired.description: The paired difference of one method against the recommended method over the same surveys.

measured.description: The measured values of the target at each survey, in survey order [t/h or kW].

methods.description: Every method with its MAPE and its per-survey errors, in the order the App lists them.

recommended.description: The method with the lowest MAPE among the methods that are not controls (a tie keeps the listing order).

runner_up.description: The method with the next lowest MAPE among the methods that are not controls.

paired.description: One paired row per method with per-survey predictions, other than the recommended one.

target.description: The comparison on one measured target.

paper.description: Authors, year and title of the source publication.

doi.description: The DOI of the source publication.

license.description: The licence of the source data, which the derived document carries.

table.description: The table of the source publication the survey rows are transcribed from.
